name: Sixtyfour
summary: Research agents and data for people and companies: enrichment, email and phone finding, reverse lookups and filter search.

api_key.description: a Sixtyfour API key starting api_ (app dashboard, Get an API Key)

notes: Credit-priced; see the notes per call and the Credit Costs page. Each key belongs to one team and counts toward its monthly spend limit.
Long research runs are async: the -async endpoints return a task_id, poll GET /job-status/{task_id}. Bulk and Atlas investigation endpoints exist but are not listed.
The lead and struct fields are free-form objects: struct maps each field you want to a description of it.

endpoints.name: Research a person (sync)
endpoints.summary: Research one person and return the fields you ask for, with sources.

lead_info.description: What you know about the person: any of name, title, company, location, linkedin, email.

struct.description: The fields to return, as {field_name: description of what to find}.

tier.description: Research depth, default low. micro up to 10 fields, medium deeper; high and scout (people) are on request.

research_plan.description: Plain-language guidance on where and how to look, up to 100,000 chars.

field_confidence.description: Return a confidence score, justification and sources for every field.

webhook_url.description: HTTPS URL that receives the result by POST when the job finishes.

notes: A read over POST.
Credits by tier per record: micro 0.3, low 1, medium 20; high and scout cost more and are on request. Use the async form in production.

endpoints.name: Research a person (async)
endpoints.summary: Same as people.intelligence but returns a task_id to poll.

lead_info.description: What you know about the person: any of name, title, company, location, linkedin, email.

endpoints.name: Read a LinkedIn profile into fields
endpoints.summary: Extract the fields you name from one LinkedIn profile, without researching other sources.

struct.description: Fields to extract, {name: description}. Without it a default set (name, headline, current company, skills, ...) is returned.

notes: A read over POST. Sync only.

endpoints.name: Find a person's email
endpoints.summary: A verified work or personal email.

lead.description: The person: a LinkedIn URL, or a name with company or domain.

mode.description: PROFESSIONAL finds a work address, PERSONAL a personal one. Default PROFESSIONAL.

verify_emails.description: Check addresses with the mail server; default true.

notes: A read over POST.
Lead field names are matched loosely: linkedin or linkedin_url, name or first_name and last_name, company or company_name, domain or website.
0.5 credits per lead with an email found (2 for personal). Status per address is OK, RISKY or UNKNOWN.

endpoints.name: Verify an email address
endpoints.summary: Whether an address can receive mail: OK, RISKY, INVALID or UNKNOWN, with a 0 to 100 score.
notes: A read over POST.
0.1 credits per request.

endpoints.name: Find the person behind an email
endpoints.summary: Name, title, employer and LinkedIn profile for an email address.
notes: A read over POST.
0.5 credits per match found.

endpoints.name: Find a person's phone number
endpoints.summary: A phone number for a person; not verified.

lead.description: The person: a LinkedIn URL, or a name with company.

notes: A read over POST.
Lead field names are matched loosely: linkedin or linkedin_url, name or first_name and last_name, company or company_name, domain or website.
3 credits per lead with a number found.

endpoints.name: Find the person behind a phone number
endpoints.summary: Name, location, email, employer and LinkedIn for a number.

lead.description: The lead, with a phone number.

notes: A read over POST.
3 credits per match found.

endpoints.name: Search people or companies
endpoints.summary: Structured, filter-based or natural-language search over Sixtyfour's people and company data, paged by cursor.

simple_filters.description: Mongo-style filters ($eq, $in, $gte, $match, $and ...) on field names from search.filter_capabilities.

filters.description: JSON query DSL (bool, term, range, ...) for what simple_filters cannot say.

query.description: A natural-language query; cannot combine with the filter forms.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous response; send it alone for the next page.

exclude_entity_ids.description: Identifiers to drop: LinkedIn public ids or URLs (people), company ids (company).

exclude_list_ids.description: Saved exclusion list ids to apply.

notes: A read over POST. Give exactly one of simple_filters, filters, query, parsed_query or search_id.
0.1 credits per result returned.
Rely on has_more and next_cursor; a page can be short while more remain.

endpoints.name: List searchable fields
endpoints.summary: Which fields are queryable, sortable and rangeable, and the filter limits, for a search mode.
notes: Use it before building filters.

endpoints.name: Get top values of a field
endpoints.summary: The most common values of a field, with ready-made filter snippets.
notes: A read over POST.
